newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors begin questioning Arizona governor.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors begin questioning Arizona governor.

text.p: Prosecutors opened their attack on embattled Arizona Gov. Fife Symington in federal court late Friday, painting him as a hands-on developer who was well paid for his efforts.
With rapid-fire questions, prosecutors began their attempt to depict Symington as a man who knew what he was doing when he allegedly defrauded lenders from the mid-1980s to the early 1990s.
They showed that the two-term governor received more than $2 million extra for his work from March 1987 through December 1989, not counting his $100,000 annual salary.
The government is expected to take several more days cross-examining Symington as it tries to prove he is guilty of 22 counts of fraud, attempted extortion and perjury.
If convicted on even a single count, the 51-year-old Republican would be ousted from the office he has held since 1991. He could face a possible prison term.

In earlier testimony Friday, Symington continued to maintain that he did nothing wrong in his financial reports and issued no threats to extort concessions from labour unions, as the government has alleged. The unions provided the money for a shopping centre in downtown Phoenix.

He also denied contentions that he lied in federal bankruptcy testimony, saying he was being honest at the time. Symington filed for Chapter 7, which usually leads to the liquidation of a company, in September 1995.
The jury could get the case in early August.
